chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan Al-Farsi, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah dislikes for you, O community, twenty-four characteristics and forbids you from them. He dislikes for you frivolity/playfulness during the prayer.'

key_terms.الْعَبَثَ: Frivolity, playfulness, or lack of seriousness

ai.seo_question: What are the twenty-four characteristics Allah dislikes for the community according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Farsi, underscores the Prophetic emphasis on khushu' (humility) by identifying 'abath' (frivolity or lack of seriousness) as a primary spiritual defect. In Shia scholarly tradition, this serves as a foundational text for the jurisprudence of prayer, linking the internal state of the worshiper to the validity and perfection of the ritual. The enumeration of twenty-four traits highlights a comprehensive approach to purifying the believer's conduct both within and beyond the prayer niche.
